I've farmed these 9 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years, and finishing school taught me to keep my own books and calculate input costs against output prices. Last year my wheat made about 460 kg per mu, which was acceptable, but my maize only reached 500 kg because I skimped on the second irrigation during that dry spell in July. Old Wang from the east village hit 580 kg on his maize because he watered at tasseling, so I learned my lesson. My soil is loamy but after decades of cropping the potassium is getting thin, especially where I grow cotton. I did a soil test through the county extension two years ago, and it showed adequate phosphorus but low potassium. I divide my 9 mu into 6 mu of wheat-maize rotation and 3 mu of cotton. With just my wife and me at 66 years old, I cannot manage more cotton because the picking and spraying are too labor-intensive. For the winter wheat already in the ground since last October, I sowed an improved variety — not the most expensive certified seed, but a reliable stock that costs 4 yuan per jin. I applied base fertilizer last autumn, and this spring I will top-dress with urea at the jointing stage. My total nutrient budget for wheat is 16 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus pentoxide, and 5 kg potassium oxide per mu. I will irrigate three times from my well: green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Electricity costs 0.6 yuan per kilowatt-hour and each irrigation runs about 15 kW, so three times is roughly 27 yuan per mu — I figure that is the minimum to protect the yield. For summer maize, I will plant a hybrid variety, probably Zhengdan 958 or something similar that the dealer recommends, sown directly into the wheat stubble with no-tillage. No-till saves me about 100 yuan per mu in tillage costs and preserves soil moisture, which matters in June when the heat comes fast. I will apply 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. Two irrigations: one at the big trumpet stage and one at tasseling-silking. Two pesticide sprays: a pre-emergence herbicide and one insecticide for corn borer. Cotton is different. It needs more potassium, so I push that to 10 kg per mu, with 13 kg nitrogen and 5 kg phosphorus. I use a Bt hybrid to cut down on bollworm, but I still need four sprays for aphids, spider mites, and weeds. I irrigate three times: budding, peak flowering, and boll filling. I expect 280 kg per mu of seed cotton if the weather cooperates. I always budget a small margin on fertilizer because a deficiency is a disaster I cannot recover from, but over-application only wastes some money. My total fertilizer and chemical bill will be around 3,200 yuan this year. That is a big outlay, but if wheat hits 480 kg/mu, maize 550 kg/mu, and cotton 280 kg/mu, I will clear enough to make it worthwhile. I checked with three neighbors and they are doing similar rates, so I feel confident.
